t: This is Battersea Central Library, on Lavender Hill in south-west London. The Battersea Vestry built it between 1889 and 1890, and it is still a working public library today, run as one of Wandsworth Council's libraries. It was designed by Edward Mountford, an architect noted for his Edwardian Baroque style. He also designed the town halls of Sheffield, Battersea and Lancaster, and the Old Bailey in London. He died young, at fifty-two, and was remembered as a very able and distinguished architect.
